subject.title: feat(talk): enable GPT Live with Codex OAuth

question: Should OpenClaw support an automatic, experimental bundled Codex OAuth fallback for browser and iOS OpenAI Realtime Talk when no authored OpenAI Platform credential exists?
rationale: The code intentionally changes a user-facing authentication and support boundary without adding an opt-in setting; tests and live proof can establish mechanics, but they cannot decide the long-term product commitment.

options.title: Accept the fallback boundary
options.body: Approve the internal Codex OAuth browser/iOS fallback, retain Platform-first precedence, and require a final merge-head compatibility check.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep Codex OAuth unavailable by default and redesign the feature around a maintainer-approved user-visible activation path.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause this PR until owners define support, lifecycle, and troubleshooting expectations for this bundled dependency path.

recommendation.title: Accept the fallback boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the internal Codex OAuth browser/iOS fallback, retain Platform-first precedence, and require a final merge-head compatibility check.

likelyOwner.reason: They can supply the final technical context and proof, while a repository owner must make the actual product decision.
